prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2025-12-18. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.71 |
| Retained earnings       | 9,761M |
| Current liabilities     | 18,514M |
| Current assets          | 31,573M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 81,292M |
| Total liabilities       | 89,800M |
| Total assets            | 171,092M |
| EBIT / operating income | 7,508M |
| Revenue                 | 18,015M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2025-12-18, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company exhibits a healthy current ratio of 1.71, indicating good short-term liquidity. However, the debt-to-equity ratio is high at 1.10 (89,800M / 81,292M), suggesting significant leverage. The interest coverage ratio (EBIT/Interest Expense) cannot be calculated without interest expense, but the EBIT margin is 41.68% (7,508M / 18,015M), which is strong. The high leverage is a concern, but the strong profitability and liquidity mitigate some of the risk.

DECISION: BBB
